title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues an elementary set-up (bracketed paragraph (13)) for the modular description of elliptic curves. The goal is to describe complex structures on a real vector space V of rank 2, the real space underlying a lattice quotient C/Λ, in several equivalent ways.

(1) Group-theoretic description. A complex structure on V is equivalent to two pieces of data:
- 1°) a compact (maximal) subgroup U ⊂ Aut_R(V), isomorphic to the circle 𝕌 = {z ∈ C : |z| = 1}, such that the action on V_C has exactly two eigenspaces;
- 2°) one of the two elements of order 4 of U. Equivalently, this is an isomorphism U ≅ 𝕌, or an orientation of U, or an orientation of V.
The element of order 4 attached to an orientation ω is written u_ω; it is the rotation by +π/2 for ω.

(2) Invariant metric. When rank V = 2, a Euclidean (unitary) structure invariant under U exists and is unique up to a positive scalar.

(3) Eigenspace decomposition. Under U, V_C splits as (14) V_C = ⊕_{ω∈ω(U)} L_ω, one line for each orientation. U acts on L_ω through a character, giving the isomorphism (15) φ_ω : U ≅ 𝕌 with g(z) = φ_ω(g)·z for z ∈ L_ω. The two characters are complex conjugate.

(4) Recovering the complex structure. Giving a complex structure is the same as choosing one of the two isomorphisms φ_ω. This lets 𝕌, and then R_{>0}^× × 𝕌 ≅ C^*, act on V, which yields C as a ring of operators. Because Re is U-equivariant, Re(φ_ω(g)z) = Re(gz) = g·Re(z). Hence Re : L_ω → V is C-linear for the complex structure c_ω; the next page states that it is an isomorphism.

(5) Higher rank (marginal note). For rank_R V = 2n, the two elements of order 4 (J and −J) determine opposite orientations exactly when n is odd. Only then is the choice equivalent to an orientation of V.

(6) Where this leads. On the next page, complex structures on V are identified with points of P(V)(C) \ P(V)(R), i.e. two copies of the half-plane. This is the standard start of the analytic description of the moduli of elliptic curves, and the complex structure is normalised by the convention of the previous page (V as a quotient by Λ, with holomorphic and antiholomorphic forms).
errors: Small imprecision: the phrase 'unique à scalaire multiplicatif près' for the invariant Euclidean structure holds only for rank 2. Grothendieck restricts it to rank 2 in an insertion, so this is consistent.

In higher rank the condition 'exactly two eigenspaces' should be complemented by requiring the two characters to be mutually inverse with equal multiplicities. This is automatic, since the space is real and the subgroup is a circle with faithful action.
The marginal claim (orientation ↔ order-4 element only when n is odd) is correct, because the orientations of J and −J differ by (−1)^n.

ideas.what: Complex structure on a real 2-plane equals a circle subgroup of GL(V) plus a choice of order-4 element (equivalently an orientation)
ideas.modern_name: Complex structures J with J² = −1; GL_2(R)/C^* ≅ P^1(C) \ P^1(R)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Riemann/Weil-era linear algebra; e.g. Weil, Variétés kählériennes)

ideas.what: Eigenspace decomposition V_C = L ⊕ L̄ under U, with Re : L → V a C-linear isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Hodge decomposition of type (1,0)+(0,1) for a rank-2 real Hodge structure; Deligne torus action
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Deligne torus formulation (Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, 1971)

ideas.what: Orientation determined by J versus −J depends on the parity of n in rank 2n
ideas.modern_name: Orientation induced by a complex structure; conjugate structure reverses orientation iff n is odd

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but entirely classical linear algebra: complex structures on R², circle actions, and the Hodge-type eigenspace decomposition, preparing the half-plane description of elliptic curve moduli. The only small extras (the parity-of-n remark, and the C^* ≅ R_{>0}^× × 𝕌 'Deligne torus' flavour) are well known.
transcription_corrections: The left-margin insertion at the top reads '(c'est-à-dire, ce qui revient au même, si rg_R V = 2)'. It likely qualifies 'compact maximal subgroup' or 'isomorphic to 𝕌', not the start of the sentence.
'𝓡' in the last lines denotes Re (real part), as confirmed by the next page ('z ↦ Re z').
'structure multiplicative [?]' is probably 'structure euclidienne' or 'unitaire' (an invariant inner product, unique up to a scalar factor), not a multiplicative structure.
'ou [?] R^{*+}_× 𝕌 ≃ C^*' should read 'par conséquent R_+^* × 𝕌 ≃ C^*, donc C ...'.
'Ceci donne aussi dit' should be 'Ceci dit' (a line break).
